messages.author: 5a363da2ae84b3c2
messages.subject: Transpose operator problem
parts:
ln_theta_hat <- ln_theta_hat_t’; //note: transpose operator at the end!

The code will compile and attempt to execute, however, when it gets to the transpose operator, it kicks back this error: 
error in call to assign; require matching dimensions, but found arg1(rows=9,cols=153); arg2(rows=153,cols=9)Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.

It appears that stan doesn't recognize/interpret the transpose operator correctly in this location. Perhaps I've typed it wrong? I'm uncertain what key, precisely, I need to push.

The full code is below. 

I've reworked the problem again and again and the error must be at this line location because this is the only place with 9 x 153 or 153 x 9 matrices. If I omit the transpose & assignment command, the code works (until it has to compute the log prob of an empty matrix)!

Thank you
David

m4.code <- '
data{
int<lower=1> months; // number of time units: months
int<lower=1> sectors; // number of observational units: sectors
int<lower=0> y[sectors, months]; // response.
int<lower=1> X_features; // number of features in X
matrix[months, X_features] X; // features matrix X
row_vector<lower=0>[months] ln_day_offset; // offset for variable-length months
}
parameters{
vector[X_features] mu;
row_vector<lower=0>[X_features] tau;
matrix[X_features, sectors] eta;
}
transformed parameters{
matrix[X_features, sectors] beta_hat;
matrix[months, sectors] ln_theta_hat_t;
matrix[sectors, months] ln_theta_hat;
for(x in 1:X_features){
beta_hat[x] <- tau*eta +mu[x]; // 
}
ln_theta_hat_t <- X*beta_hat; 
ln_theta_hat <- ln_theta_hat_t’; //note: transpose operator at the end!
}
model{
mu ~ student_t(3,0,1);
for (s in 1:sectors){
eta[s] ~ normal(0,1);
y[s] ~ poisson_log(ln_theta_hat[s]+ln_day_offset); 
}
}
generated quantities{
matrix[sectors, months] theta_hat;
theta_hat <- exp(ln_theta_hat);
}
'
## this is fake data, but it should work fine
sector.apps <- matrix(rpois(9*153, lambda=10), ncol=9, nrow=153)
days.in.month <- sample(c(29,28,30,31), size=153, replace=T)
X <- cbind(1, rexp(153, rate=1/10))

m4.dat <- list( months= 153,
sectors= 9,
y= t(as.matrix(sector.apps)),
X= X,
X_features= 2,
ln_day_offset= log(sub.data[,days.in.month]))

You've declared ln_theta_hat_t as:

If months != sectors, you can't just transpose and set ln_theta_hat_t with its transpose.

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Transpose operator problem
parts:
Hi David,

Sorry about that last post -- I was incorrect in assuming that was the problem.

I think this is an R issue. You're used a backtick for transpose instead of a single quotation mark. I'd suggest writing your model in a separate file. If you're not willing to do that, you'll have to escape the single quote. For whatever reason, our parser allows the backtick and just ignores it.


Daniel

I'll get off of my soapbox and leave these decisions to the professionals now.

Thanks again -- I'm very appreciative for the feedback.

messages.author: 0839befa8a8b7d53
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Transpose operator problem
parts:
Seems like there's some crosstalk here. 

The parser isn't the problem. The problem is that the transpose symbol is a single quote ' instead of the slanted accent symbol  ´.

But since you quoted your model code within single quote marks, you can't use a single quote mark within the model code.

To fix this, just use double quotes " to enclose your model code. Then replace the ´ with ' for the transposition.

On Thursday, June 12, 2014 2:03:17 PM UTC-7, dje wrote:
Thanks again, Daniel! I just ran the toy problem and it kicked the same error, so it must indeed be the parser... I'll look into how to escape the character in R, as you suggested.

I know that you're probably not eager for additional user-submitted suggestions (I rarely am), but I've never had this problem with R's t() command for transpose. I appreciate the similarity between the backtick and the mathematical transpose mark, but I must wonder if it's worth it. 

I'll get off of my soapbox and leave these decisions to the professionals now.

Thanks again -- I'm very appreciative for the feedback.


On Thu, Jun 12, 2014 at 4:58 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
Hi David,

Sorry about that last post -- I was incorrect in assuming that was the problem.

I think this is an R issue. You're used a backtick for transpose instead of a single quotation mark. I'd suggest writing your model in a separate file. If you're not willing to do that, you'll have to escape the single quote. For whatever reason, our parser allows the backtick and just ignores it.


Daniel


On Thu, Jun 12, 2014 at 4:28 PM, Daniel Lee <bea...@alum.mit.edu> wrote:
Hi dje,

Stan's matrix sizes are fixed. We should be stopping Stan with a different error message, but we haven't put that in yet.

You've declared ln_theta_hat_t as:
matrix[months, sectors] ln_theta_hat_t;

If months != sectors, you can't just transpose and set ln_theta_hat_t with its transpose.

ln_theta_hat <- ln_theta_hat_t’; //note: transpose operator at the end!

The code will compile and attempt to execute, however, when it gets to the transpose operator, it kicks back this error: 
error in call to assign; require matching dimensions, but found arg1(rows=9,cols=153); arg2(rows=153,cols=9)Rejecting proposed initial value with zero density.

It appears that stan doesn't recognize/interpret the transpose operator correctly in this location. Perhaps I've typed it wrong? I'm uncertain what key, precisely, I need to push.

The full code is below. 

I've reworked the problem again and again and the error must be at this line location because this is the only place with 9 x 153 or 153 x 9 matrices. If I omit the transpose & assignment command, the code works (until it has to compute the log prob of an empty matrix)!

Thank you
David

m4.code <- '
data{
int<lower=1> months; // number of time units: months
int<lower=1> sectors; // number of observational units: sectors
int<lower=0> y[sectors, months]; // response.
int<lower=1> X_features; // number of features in X
matrix[months, X_features] X; // features matrix X
row_vector<lower=0>[months] ln_day_offset; // offset for variable-length months
}
parameters{
vector[X_features] mu;
row_vector<lower=0>[X_features] tau;
matrix[X_features, sectors] eta;
}
transformed parameters{
matrix[X_features, sectors] beta_hat;
matrix[months, sectors] ln_theta_hat_t;
matrix[sectors, months] ln_theta_hat;
for(x in 1:X_features){
beta_hat[x] <- tau*eta +mu[x]; // 
}
ln_theta_hat_t <- X*beta_hat; 
ln_theta_hat <- ln_theta_hat_t’; //note: transpose operator at the end!
}
model{
mu ~ student_t(3,0,1);
for (s in 1:sectors){
eta[s] ~ normal(0,1);
y[s] ~ poisson_log(ln_theta_hat[s]+ln_day_offset); 
}
}
generated quantities{
matrix[sectors, months] theta_hat;
theta_hat <- exp(ln_theta_hat);
}
'
## this is fake data, but it should work fine
sector.apps <- matrix(rpois(9*153, lambda=10), ncol=9, nrow=153)
days.in.month <- sample(c(29,28,30,31), size=153, replace=T)
X <- cbind(1, rexp(153, rate=1/10))

m4.dat <- list( months= 153,
sectors= 9,
y= t(as.matrix(sector.apps)),
X= X,
X_features= 2,
ln_day_offset= log(sub.data[,days.in.month]))
